message:
feat(directory): the server says where observations go, instead of the client guessing

Clients derived the observe port as httpPort + 1. That holds only while the
directory is reached directly on its own two ports. Behind a TLS terminator
on 443 it becomes 444, nothing listens there, and observation fails -- and a
host whose observation fails skips its heartbeat, so it never appears in
the list at all. The relay is no help: its address arrives in the
/api/connect response, and the viewer returns before it ever calls connect.

So the server advertises the endpoint as optional metadata on responses the
client already reads -- login, host register, healthz. No new route, and an
older client that does not look for it is unaffected. The advertised port
is configuration rather than a derivation, because a NAT mapping or a proxy
can present something other than the listen port; unset, it is the listen
port. A value outside 1..65535 is not advertised at all, since a wrong port
is worse than none: none leaves the client on a documented fallback, wrong
sends it somewhere that will never answer and reads as a network fault.

On the client the endpoint is not a new path. Both C++ clients already had
an explicit override that wins over the default, so this fills those in.
The rules differ by scheme deliberately: what the server said always wins;
plain http with no metadata keeps the +1 default every existing deployment
relies on; https with no metadata yields nothing at all. It does not quietly
try 443 + 1, and it does not fall back to a fixed 29181 -- both are guesses
that cannot be right, and either would turn "this server needs configuring"
into a silent timeout. The host reports that state instead and does not
probe a socket it has not been able to aim.

The nested read is deliberate too. A flat search for "port" finds the first
one anywhere in the response; that is unambiguous in today's replies and
would not stay so, and the failure would be a wrong port rather than an
error.
